subject: Invoice rhythm, tax withholding, and credit cap — SparkBridge pilot
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Costa <ana.costa@sparkbridge.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed invoicing rhythm & VAT certificate request for pilot (SB-9843)

Hi Ana —

Great to kick off the pilot with SparkBridge last week. To unblock billing for the next two months, attached is a proposed invoice rhythm (redwood_invoice_schedule_v2.xlsx) that maps expected usage milestones to invoice dates. A few asks from our side so finance can set up the account: 

- Requested net terms: Net45 from invoice date. This aligns with our standard for pilots of this size and gives both teams predictable cash flow.
- Temporary credit cap: we propose a soft cap of $200,000 for the pilot window; once spend pattern is established we can reevaluate.
- VAT handling: since SparkBridge is EU-registered, can you confirm whether you will be providing a valid VAT certificate? If so, Redwood will apply reverse-charge where applicable and not remit VAT on those invoices. If not, we will need to include VAT on our invoices per local rules.
- Preferred payment methods: SEPA or SWIFT wire; we can accept ACH for US entities.

I've copied Marissa from finance to confirm the credit-cap mechanics and reconciliation cadence. If these terms look reasonable, please reply with your VAT certificate attached and any counter-proposals on payment timing.

Thanks and looking forward —

Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_invoice_schedule_v2.xlsx
From: Ana Costa <ana.costa@sparkbridge.io>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: SparkBridge Accounting <acct@sparkbridge.io>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:46:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Proposed invoicing rhythm & VAT certificate request for pilot (SB-9843)

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the schedule — this is helpful. A couple of notes from SparkBridge finance: 

- Net terms: Our standard is Net60 for new vendors during pilots. Is there flexibility to move to Net60 for the first 60 days and then reprice to Net45 thereafter?
- Credit cap: we can commit to a €170,000 limit (we operate in EUR). Does Redwood need that denominated in USD?
- VAT: attaching our VAT registration (sparkbridge_vat_certificate.pdf). We confirm we're a B2B EU entity; please apply reverse-charge where applicable.
- Payment method: SEPA preferred for EUR invoices.

If Redwood requires specific contract language for VAT reverse charge or a withholding waiver, please flag and we'll route to legal.

Best,
Ana Costa
Head of Finance Ops — SparkBridge
ana.costa@sparkbridge.io

Attachments: sparkbridge_vat_certificate.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ana Costa <ana.costa@sparkbridge.io>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 08:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed invoicing rhythm & VAT certificate request for pilot (SB-9843)

Stephanie / Monica —

Reviewed Ana's reply and certificate. Quick internal notes and proposed operational flow: 

- Currency: SparkBridge prefers EUR; we'll issue EUR-denominated invoices and record the accounting in USD per our FX policy. For the credit cap, we'll translate €170,000 to USD using the day-of-invoice FX rate and surface both values on the invoice.
- Terms: Acceptable compromise — Net60 for the first two invoices (pilot ramp), then Net45 for subsequent invoices. We'll flag this as a staged-term in billing permissions.
- Credit cap: We'll put a soft credit cap of $180,000 USD equivalent (to give a slight buffer vs their €170k), with automated alerts at 70%/90% consumption. No hard-cutoff for the pilot, finance escalation required before suspension.
- VAT/reverse charge: Certificate looks valid. We will apply reverse-charge on B2B line items and include the mandatory wording on the invoice. No withholding should be taken by SparkBridge if they have supplied this certificate.
- Payment instructions: SEPA details in the attached invoice schedule. For any late payments beyond Net60+10 grace, we will assess a standard interest charge (per contract).

I attached the updated invoice rhythm (redwood_invoice_schedule_v2.xlsx) with the staged Net60->Net45 timeline and the currency notes. Stephanie, please send Ana the updated schedule and the confirmation email for signature.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_invoice_schedule_v2.xlsx
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Costa <ana.costa@sparkbridge.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed invoicing rhythm & VAT certificate request for pilot (SB-9843)

Hi Ana —

Thanks for confirming the VAT certificate and the €170k figure. Per Marissa / Monica's notes, summary of agreed items for the pilot: 

- Invoice cadence & terms: Issue monthly EUR invoices. Net60 for invoices dated Dec/Jan (first two), then Net45 for Feb onward.
- Credit cap: Soft cap at $180,000 USD equivalent; Redwood will send threshold alerts at 70% and 90% consumption. No automatic suspension without manual escalation.
- VAT: We'll apply reverse-charge on B2B line items. No VAT will be charged provided the certificate remains valid. We will include the standard reverse-charge clause and your VAT number on each invoice.
- Payment method: SEPA transfers to Redwood's EUR account. Wire instructions will be included on invoices.

Would you please reply with a short confirmation and attach the signed MOU (if you'd like it recorded)? I've attached a signed copy of the minimal MOU we use for pilots (signed_mou.pdf) for your records.

If you confirm, we'll kick off billing on the next invoice cycle (invoice on Jan 1 for December usage).

Best regards,

Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

Attachments: signed_mou.pdf
